Volochysk Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the older of Volochysk's two Jewish cemeteries. Jews began settling in Volochysk in the 18th century, numbering 384 in 1765 and reaching 3,295 (49.1 percent) by 1897; the town's synagogue count grew from three in 1863 to eight by 1890. Following anti-Jewish riots on May 4-5, 1881, units of Jewish self-defense were formed. During WWII, a ghetto was created after the July 1941 occupation; the source's own account of the 1942 death tolls is unclear, citing both roughly 8,634 and approximately 4,000 Jews killed in separate actions that August and September, a discrepancy flagged here rather than resolved. Volochysk-born notable figures include Meir Benihu (1896–1981), an Israeli journalist who edited major Hebrew-language publications including Ha'aretz and Davar; David Margolis (born 1911), a sculptor and painter whose interior paintings include work in New York's Rockefeller Center; and Isaac Tartakovsky (born 1912), a Merited Artist of the USSR whose 1991 painting 'Requiem' depicted the Babi Yar massacre.
